interface.title: PTMVision – Interactive Exploration of Post Translational Modifications
interface.stage_of_work: Downstream exploration and interpretation of PTM identification results from search engines
interface.what_it_is_for: Turn PTM search results from many search engines into a combined overview of modification types, mass shifts and co-occurrences, plus a protein table you can filter, and (when structures can be fetched) per-protein sequence, structure and contact-map views.

data.note: I loaded the bundled ionbot (E. coli; 1992 modifications, 150 types), Plain/CSV (IEEE VIS 2022 human/mouse; 2618 modifications, 173 types), PeptideAtlas (P0AA16; 28 modifications) and MSFragger examples. The replay noticed that the MSFragger example, labelled human, loaded a table of archaeal A0A0U3… proteins (7617 modifications, 67 types). I also uploaded the test file ptmvision_example.csv as Plain/CSV, but the server rejected it with a parse error (see not_done). The server has no network, so it could not fetch AlphaFold structures, and the per-protein detail view never opened for any protein. The bundled examples evidently do not embed structures.

features.name: Linked multi-chart overview with category highlighting
features.general: A row of charts sharing one category axis (pairwise co-occurrence heatmap, value scatter, count bars). You pick categories in a searchable multi-select, and guide lines mark them in every chart at once.
features.specific: In the Overview PTMs panel, press Highlight PTM, search and pick UniMod modification names (e.g. Oxidation, Dioxidation) and press OK. Dashed labelled lines then appear across the Shared PTM Sites heatmap, the Mass shift plot and the Site count bars.
steps: press Highlight PTM
type part of a name in the dialog's search box
pick one or more modification types as chips
press OK and read the labelled guide lines in all three charts
serves_tasks: Mark chosen modification types across all linked charts
See which modification types share sites and how often each occurs

features.name: Co-occurrence heatmap with zoom, sort and label density controls
features.general: A category-by-category matrix of shared items. You can wheel-zoom it, reset it, reorder it by count or by a numeric property and switch between auto and all axis labels. Hover tooltips give the pair and its count.
features.specific: Shared PTM Sites between Modification Types: wheel-zoom, Reset zoom, Sort by count/mass shift, Show all/auto labels. Hovering a cell reads e.g. '53 sites have been modified by both Oxidation (15.99 Da) and Carboxy->Thiocarboxy'.
steps: scroll the wheel over the heatmap to zoom into a region
hover a cell to read the pair and its shared-site count
press Sort by count/mass shift to reorder rows and columns
press Show all/auto labels to toggle label density
press Reset zoom to return to the full view
serves_tasks: See which modification types share sites and how often each occurs
Reorder and declutter the overview charts

features.name: Filterable, sortable entity table with single-row selection (hand-off to detail view unverified)
features.general: A table of items, one row each with summary counts. Two searchable multi-select filters narrow it (by attribute and by name/ID), and any column sorts it. You click one row to select it; a Display button is meant to send that row to a detail panel.
features.specific: Select Single Protein of Interest: filter by UniMod modification name and/or protein name/UniProt ID, sort by sequence length, modified positions or distinct modifications, and click a row (it turns red). Pressing Display to fill Explore Detail was not verified: it returned 'Status 500: Alphafold structure not available' for every protein tried.
steps: pick a modification in 'Filter for modifications by UniMod name'
optionally pick a protein in 'Filter for protein names/UniProt identifier'
click a column header to sort
click a row to select it (unverified next step: press Display to open Explore Detail)
serves_tasks: Rank proteins by how heavily they are modified
Narrow the table to proteins carrying one modification type
Find a specific protein by name or accession

features.name: Ready-made example sessions (upload-and-submit route unverified)
features.general: Start an analysis by launching one of several pre-built example datasets from a table. Beside it is a form for choosing an input format, uploading a file, excluding categories and setting a matching tolerance; in this run that form never produced a loaded session.
features.specific: Panel 1: Browse Example Sessions and press Start on a row. The upload form (Input Format: ionbot, MSFragger, Sage, MaxQuant, Spectronaut, mzIdentML, Plain/CSV…; PTM Data upload; Exclude UniMod Classes; Adjust Mass Shift Tolerance, default 0.001; Submit) is present but unverified: the only upload tried was rejected with a parse error.
steps: press Browse Example Sessions
read the table of examples (search engine, organism, description)
press Start on an example row
scroll to Overview PTMs and the protein table, which now hold that dataset
serves_tasks: Load a ready-made example dataset instead of preparing files

features.name: Session export and cookie resume (file re-import unverified)
features.general: Save the entire analysis state to one compressed file. The server also keeps the session behind a browser cookie, so reopening the page restores it.
features.specific: Download Session Data saves ptmvision-<date>.zlib. Reloading the page re-initialises the last session from the cookie (filter selections are not kept). The '(Or) Re-upload a PTMVision session' input exists but was not tried, so restoring from the .zlib file is unverified.
steps: press Download Session Data in the header
keep the .zlib file
return to the page; the cookie restores the overview and protein table
serves_tasks: Export the whole analysis state as one file
Resume the previous session on returning to the page

PeptideAtlas example protein table: the overview loaded (screens/031.webp) but the protein table stayed empty (screens/032.webp, 033.jpg). A later error message about P0AA16 position '-' parsing suggests the cause.

The examples ship without embedded structures, contrary to the setup note that they were pre-baked.
Explore PTM positions along a protein's sequence and its 3D structure: same blocker.
Inspect the residue-residue contact map: same blocker.
Check UniProt/UniMod annotations for a modified residue: same blocker.

Upload ptmvision_example.csv as Plain/CSV (with Artefact excluded): Submit returned 'Failed request to get available proteins (Status 500): Failed to parse modified position - for protein P0AA16: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '-''. No overview or table appeared (screens/043.webp, 045.jpg). Class exclusion and mass-shift tolerance were therefore never seen to take effect.
